\section{Hypercontractivity --- Applications --- KKL --- Threshold}
%%% generated by the blueprint pipeline from TCSlib.BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.Applications.KKL.Threshold
\subsection*{Hypercontractivity --- Applications --- KKL --- Threshold: Introduction}
Linear threshold functions have Fourier tails controlled by a reciprocal-square degree cutoff. An optimized influence threshold gives junta approximation with polynomial dependence on total influence.

\difficulty{5}
There is a real constant $B\ge1$ such that, for every natural number $n$ and every
function $f:\{0,1\}^n\to\mathbb R$ taking only the values $-1$ and $1$ and admitting a
degree-at-most-one polynomial threshold representation, the following holds for every
$\varepsilon$ with $0<\varepsilon\le\tfrac12$: there is a natural number $k$ such that
$k\le B/\varepsilon^2$ and the Fourier weight on levels strictly above $k$ is at most
$\varepsilon$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Linear threshold junta size bound]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.linearThreshold_junta_size_bound}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.ComparisonAux.junta_polynomial_absorption}
\difficulty{5}
Let $B,\varepsilon,\eta\in\mathbb R$ satisfy $1\le B$ and $0<\varepsilon,\eta\le 1/2$.
For every $k\in\mathbb N$ with $k\le B/\varepsilon^2$, we have
$\dfrac{1}{\bigl(\varepsilon(\eta/(2+\eta))^k\bigr)^{1+\eta}}\le
(1/\eta)^{200B/\varepsilon^2}$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{theorem}[Linear-threshold junta approximation]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.linearThreshold_junta}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.BooleanFunc, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.cubeVariance, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.cubeVariance_eq_sum_nonempty_fourier, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.exists_boolean_constant_approximation, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.fourierWeightAbove_le_totalInfluence_div_succ, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.linearThreshold_fourier_cutoff, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.linearThreshold_junta_size_bound, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.optimized_junta_of_fourier_tail, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.IsClose, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.IsLinearThreshold, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.disagreementProbability, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.fourierWeightAbove, BooleanAnalysis.isPmOne, BooleanAnalysis.totalInfluence, BooleanAnalysis.totalInfluence_eq_sum_sq_deg, KKL.IsJunta}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p269-b007}
\difficulty{5}
There exists an absolute $C>0$ such that for every linear threshold function $f:\{0,1\}^n\to\{-1,1\}$ under the uniform law and $0<\varepsilon,\eta\le1/2$, there exist $J\subseteq[n]$ and $h:\{0,1\}^n\to\{-1,1\}$ depending only on $J$ with $|J|\le I(f)^{2+\eta}(1/\eta)^{C/\varepsilon^2}$ and $\Pr(f\ne h)\le\varepsilon$. For a real cube function $h$, define $I_i(h)=\tfrac14\mathbb E_x(h(x)-h(x^{(i)}))^2$, where $x^{(i)}$ flips coordinate $i$ and $\mathbb E_x$ is uniform expectation, and $I(h)=\sum_{i=0}^{n-1}I_i(h)$.
\end{theorem}
